title: Pangu-Weather: A 3D High-Resolution System for Fast and Accurate Global Weather Forecast
layout_note: Symmetric left-to-right: input fields on the far left, patch tokens, an encoder container whose two layers step down, a decoder container whose two layers step back up, then patch tokens and output fields mirrored on the far right. The U is shallow (two levels) and drawn inside two side-by-side containers.
grouping: Two thin blue-outlined square containers labelled in bold below them, 'Encoder' and 'Decoder', each holding two light-grey layer boxes stacked vertically. Inputs split into two rows, pressure-level variables above and surface variables below, each followed by a column of five small cube tokens; the two rows merge into the encoder and split out of the decoder. A bold title naming the network sits centred at the top.
shapes_depth: Data are images: pressure-level variables are three rendered 3-D cubes whose faces carry colormapped fields (blue-cyan-yellow-red), surface variables are three flat colormapped maps; tokens are small colormapped cubes in a column. Layer boxes are flat light-grey rectangles with thin dark outlines and centred text (layer name, block name with a repeat count, and the tensor size in math). Data-flow arrows are thick orange; down- and up-sampling are dotted orange vertical arrows with italic labels.
proposed_highlight: The network is named in a large bold title above the containers and the proposed block is named inside every layer box; no colour is reserved for the proposal — the colour all goes to the data fields.
lesson: Mirror the input and output fields on both sides with identical renderings (3-D cubes for pressure-level variables, flat maps for surface ones) and their tensor sizes underneath, so the model reads as field in, same field out, with a compact grey network between.
notes: venue = arXiv: the PDF is headed 'TECHNICAL REPORT' and names no venue (a later Nature paper by the same group is a separate publication; not verified here). year = arXiv preprint year (2211.02556). Many small embedded images (the field renders) were recorded by refs crop and left out of the palette.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.note: modality = gridded atmospheric fields (3-D pressure-level and 2-D surface variables)

core.what: a mirror-symmetric left-to-right pipeline: upper-air and surface fields are patch-embedded and merged into a two-level encoder, then a two-level decoder whose output is split and patch-recovered into the same two field sets

relations.form: left to right on thick orange arrows: input fields, patch tokens, Encoder, Decoder, patch tokens, output fields, mirrored about the centre
the upper-air (top) and surface (bottom) token columns converge with orange arrows labelled 'merge' onto Layer 1, and leave Layer 4 by two diverging arrows labelled 'split'
upper-air variables (three 3-D cubes) and surface variables (three flat maps) run as two stacked rows at both ends, each with its own patch embedding/recovery size

inside two blue-outlined squares, Layer 1 over Layer 2 (encoder) and Layer 4 over Layer 3 (decoder), linked by dotted orange down-sampling and up-sampling arrows and horizontal skip arrows at each level
inputs, tokens and outputs are drawn as colormapped renders of the actual atmospheric fields with tensor sizes under each

channels.colour: orange = all data-flow arrows; colormapped renders = data; grey fill = layer boxes
channels.shape: 3-D cube = upper-air field, flat map = surface field, small cubes in a column = patch tokens, grey box = a layer
channels.line: solid orange = data flow and skip, dotted orange = down/up-sampling
channels.frame: thin blue square = Encoder or Decoder group

quality.strengths: The data are drawn as data (colour-mapped field cubes and maps with their tensor sizes), the mirror layout makes input and output symmetric so the encoder-decoder reads at a glance, and line style separates resampling (dotted) from data flow (solid).
quality.weaknesses: The Earth-Specific Block, the paper's contribution, is a text label inside plain grey boxes with nothing drawn of its 3-D attention; the field renders take most of the area while the layers are small; the merge/split arrows are long diagonals across empty space.

insights.structure: Mirror-symmetric left to right: input fields and patch tokens on the far left, two thin blue-outlined square containers 'Encoder' and 'Decoder' in the middle each holding two grey layer boxes stacked vertically, then patch tokens and output fields mirrored on the far right, under a bold centred title.
insights.data: Upper-air variables are three rendered 3-D cubes with colormapped faces, surface variables three flat colormapped maps; tokens are columns of five small colormapped cubes; each layer box states block name with repeat count and tensor size in math.
insights.emphasis: Colour is spent on the real data fields while the network stays grey, and identical renderings on both sides make 'field in, same field out' visible; the model name is the large bold title.
insights.flow: Thick orange arrows run left to right, merging the two input rows into Layer 1 and splitting out of Layer 4; dotted orange vertical arrows show down-sampling in the encoder and up-sampling in the decoder.
insights.avoid: The two-level U is drawn inside two separate boxes, so the skip from Layer 1 to Layer 4 looks like an ordinary forward arrow rather than a skip connection.

arrangement.units: one composition; two thin blue-outlined square containers (Encoder, Decoder) each holding two grey layer boxes, labelled in bold below
arrangement.inputs_as: colormapped field renders (3-D cubes and flat maps) with tensor sizes underneath
